The conv on edge 5 seems to compensate, but strong parents have more to lose, while weak parents sit near the floor where pooling looks harmless.
Removing the input-output edge seems irrelevant when a conv path exists, but strong conv-chain parents depend on it for trainability and have more accuracy to lose.
A downstream conv might seem to repair pooled features, but harmful edits cost more in strong parents than in weak ones near the floor.
The conv on edge 4 looks like it should absorb the damage, but it makes the parent strong, and harmful edits bite harder in strong parents.
A strong conv elsewhere might seem to make edge 3 irrelevant, but in strong parents replacing the residual with pooling degrades more than in weak floor-level parents.
Pooling on the internal edge seems harmless when the output has a strong conv, but floor effects make harmful edits look benign only in weak parents, so strong parents lose more.
Adding depth before a strong conv seems synergistic, but headroom limits gains in parents already strong at the output.
A cheap conv might seem to complement a 3x3 conv, but parents already holding the strongest op leave little headroom for a weaker conv.
A conv on edge 0 might seem to feed a richer node 2 when edge 1 is also a conv, but redundant conv capacity saturates and leaves less room for improvement.
